## Summary

**Vulnerability:** Heap-buffer-overflow in `ndpi_int_check_stun` in `stun.c`

**Root cause:** In the STUN attribute parsing loop, the `case 0x0014` (Realm) handler reads a length field from the packet and then copies that many bytes from the payload into `flow->host_server_name`. The outer loop only checks that the 4-byte attribute header (`offset+2 < payload_length`) is within bounds, but there was no check that the actual realm data (starting at `offset+4`) was fully contained in the payload. A crafted STUN packet with a Realm attribute claiming a large length would cause reads past the end of the heap-allocated payload buffer.

**Fix:** Added a bounds check before the copy loop:
```c
/* Make sure the realm data is fully contained in the packet */
if((offset+4+realm_len) > payload_length)
  break;
```

This ensures the code only reads realm data that is actually present in the packet, preventing the heap-buffer-overflow.<tool_call><function=bash><parameter=command>echo "Fix applied successfully"</parameter><parameter=description>Confirm fix</parameter></function></tool_call>
